transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-16 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (VeraHealth Head of ML), Diane Park (VeraHealth CTO), Carlos Rivera (VeraHealth Infra Lead)
Shared artifacts: redwood/poc/benchmarks.csv (link), poc/notes.docx (drive link)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna get started, um this is our weekly sync for the POC. quick roll call?
[00:08] Sam (VeraHealth): Sam here, Sam Lee.
[00:10] Diane (VeraHealth): Diane, hi.
[00:11] Carlos (VeraHealth): Carlos on infra.
[00:13] Alex: great, priya from our side?
[00:15] Priya (Redwood SE): hey all, priya here. I will walk through the benchmark results and then we can dig into any anomalies. caveat: the CSV has raw numbers and run configs in the drive.
[00:25] Alex: quick agenda — review numbers vs your baseline provider, discuss tuning we applied (batching + kv cache + quant), look at tail latency behavior and then action items.

[00:40] Priya: ok jumping in — baseline you sent was 'Nimbus' provider (note: customer text called it "nimbis" in doc), we re-run your top-100 prompts with your sample traffic shape. two key buckets: median latency for 1-2k token responses and throughput (req/s).
[01:05] Priya: centerpiece numbers: median latency (cold) baseline ~ 240ms, Redwood hosted profile after tuning median ~ 115ms. p95 baseline ~ 680ms vs Redwood ~ 280ms. p99 baseline ~ 1.1s vs Redwood ~ 420ms. throughput: baseline plateau ~ 180 req/s, Redwood observed plateau ~ 260 req/s on the same GPU class in our Dedicated-equivalent run.
[01:33] Sam: ok that's promising. curious about test parity — were you running same model architecture + quant?
[01:40] Priya: yes, we used the same open checkpoint and a 4-bit quant profile for both; baseline run was using their default 8-bit, so interestingly we improved both latency and throughput by using our continuous batching and prefix KV cache. small note: baseline seemed to have less efficient KV handling which hit p99.

[02:05] Carlos: when you say KV cache, you mean prefix caching of the key-value (they said k-v cash in meeting), like reusing prompt context across similar requests? what about invalidation?
[02:20] Priya: exactly — prefix/KV cache. for the prompts that share the same system / instruction prefix we avoid re-computing early layers, so per-token work drops. invalidation we configured per-user session TTL 5m for this run. we also tested with a cold-cache run to show worst-case.

[02:50] Diane: any differences in hardware? baseline was using the same A100-ish class?
[02:55] Priya: we matched approximate GPU family; small variance in cuda driver and kernel versions might exist. we included instance config in the CSV. CPU + infra network variance contributed to small tail differences on the baseline. 

[03:20] Alex: also worth calling out our batching strategy — dynamic batching tuned to keep p95 under 350ms, and we prioritized latency over maximal throughput for the profile you asked. if you want more throughput we can trade off some median.

[03:40] Sam: can you show the latency-by-batch-size distribution?
[03:45] Priya: sure — so in the CSV, column B is batch size and columns show median/p95/p99. quick verbal: at batch size 8, median ~90ms, p95 ~260ms. at batch 16 median ~130ms but throughput up ~30%. beyond 32 we saw diminishing returns and p99 jumps.

[04:20] Carlos: how deterministic are these runs? do we have variance across time of day?
[04:25] Priya: good question — that's why we recommended the 24h full-profile run to capture diurnal variance and network noise. the short runs (1-2 hours) are stable but miss edge spikes.

[04:45] Alex: also, quantization — we tried both 4-bit and 8-bit. 4-bit with our kernel selection gave best latency/throughput with minimal quality regression on your eval set; we flagged a couple prompts where decoding changed, those are in the 'quality_regressions' tab in the spreadsheet.

[05:10] Sam: those are the top-5 corner-case prompts? i saw them. two of them are safety/PHI sensitive so we need to be careful.

[05:16] Priya: yep we marked those for manual review. if you'd like, we can revert to 8-bit for those classes or apply a model variant.

[05:30] Diane: on encryption and compliance — Carlos, remind them of our SSO / KMS requirements.
[05:35] Carlos: we need KMS integration, customer-managed keys, and audit logs with retention 1 year. also VPC peering or private link is required.

[05:45] Alex: noted — we'll share the SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration doc. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; we also have audit log export. will attach docs.

[06:05] Sam: can the KV cache store be in our VPC? any data residency issues?
[06:10] Priya: for Private/Dedicated yes, cache and KV store can be in your VPC. for hosted we use encrypted ephemeral stores and we can configure TTLs; full isolation is via Dedicated/Private.

[06:30] Carlos: what about tail latency mitigation? you mentioned fallback policies earlier.
[06:35] Priya: we have smart routing — we can route requests to a cheaper pool for background tasks and to a low-latency pool for live sessions. automatic fallback to a lower-capacity compatible model cuts p99 spikes. also opportunistic prefill and gradient checkpointing help.

[06:55] Alex: want to call out specific numbers from today's run: cold-start median for Redwood ~115ms, warmed median ~85ms. baseline warmed was ~210ms. p99 warmed Redwood ~360-420ms vs baseline ~1.1s. these are from the 'summary' tab in the CSV.

[07:20] Sam: so practically we see about 2x median improvement and ~3x improvement p99. that's compelling for user-facing latency SLOs. how reproducible?

[07:30] Priya: reproducible with our run configs; we'll hand over the exact CLI commands and container images. again the 24h run will prove stability under real trace.

[07:48] Diane: any cost delta? baseline's pricing structure is opaque but our cost model needs to be predictable.

[07:55] Alex: Redwood's Optimize recommendations suggest batching and caching can reduce token costs ~25-40% depending on reuse. for Dedicated pilot we can give committed throughput pricing so your unit economics are predictable. we'll include a sample TCO sheet.

[08:18] Carlos: edge case — some prompts are long (4k tokens). how does the runtime behave?

[08:23] Priya: long-seq performance drops linearly but our kernel selection and KV cache still helps because we avoid recomputing the prefix. for 4k tokens median increased as expected, p99 saw larger variance; we documented specific numbers in the long_tokens tab.

[08:45] Sam: ok next, anomalies — there was one spike around minute 42 in your run, any idea?

[08:50] Priya: yes, we saw a network interrupt on the node causing a small GC and container restart — we annotated that sample in the CSV and removed it from the baseline median, but we kept the p99 to be conservative.

[09:10] Alex: question for you, Sam — what's your success criteria for this POC at end of pilot?

[09:16] Sam: three things: 1) consistent median <150ms for our interactive UI 2) p99 <500ms for 99% of live traffic 3) cost per session below our current baseline by at least 10% or predictable committed pricing.

[09:35] Alex: good, we can meet those with Dedicated pilot tuning and the 24h run. we'll propose a config that targets those SLOs.

[09:45] Carlos: for the 24h run we need to decide instance types and whether to test Dedicated-equivalent vs hosted.

[09:52] Priya: propose two runs: 1) hosted-equivalent (our managed pool) to validate quick wins, 2) Dedicated-equivalent with your VPC settings to measure isolation and tail. we can orchestrate both.

[10:10] Diane: timeline? we need results before C-level review end of month.

[10:14] Alex: agreed — we'll aim to have the 24h run and results by 2025-07-23 so you can review before month-end.

[10:25] Priya: any more technical deep-dive items? I can share flame graphs and kernel-level timings if you want.

[10:30] Sam: yes please — flame graphs would help Carlos and our infra team.

[10:38] Carlos: also share the exact CUDA / driver versions used so we can match.

[10:41] Priya: will include CUDA, driver, libc, and kernel details in the run config.

[10:50] Alex: quick notes on next steps — we'll upload the bench CSV and run configs, share security docs, schedule the 24h run (Priya + Carlos), and draft a Dedicated pilot pricing.

[11:03] Diane: sounds good. one more question — are we comfortable with model updates during pilot? we need version pinning.

[11:10] Priya: you can pin model versions & rollout policies; Redwood supports canary and automatic fallback if we detect quality regressions.

[11:25] Sam: ok thanks everyone. we'll wait for the CSV and security pack.

[11:29] Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up with action items in the doc and set the 24h run calendar invite.

[11:34] Priya: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
